findings.description: The workflow throws only when Invoke-Pester's FailedCount is greater than zero. A BeforeAll or AfterAll container failure can leave FailedCount at zero while Result is Failed; the repository's full registry explicitly documents and handles this case at tests/f198-regression-suite.ps1:209-211. The matrix can therefore remain green when a changed volume-oracle suite fails during setup or teardown, potentially with the new measurement absent. This is the lane identified as the path-identity certification instrument. Require Result to equal Passed (or otherwise include failed-container state) for every suite.
findings.title: The three-OS certification lane can pass failed Pester containers

findings.description: Get-ConsumerAssumptionSurface returns FileInfo entries through Sort-Object FullName -Unique. Sort-Object uses a case-insensitive, culture-aware string comparison by default, so a case-sensitive worktree containing docs/Policy.md and docs/policy.md can lose one file before scanning. An unqualified technology or delivery mandate in the discarded file then produces no advisory finding, violating the FR-046 applicability firewall. The path-dedup structural test also misses this spelling because it matches only Sort-Object followed immediately by -Unique. Deduplicate file identities ordinally and add a case-distinct fixture.
findings.title: Consumer applicability scanning drops case-distinct files

summary: Risk-based review completed. Both controller-declared verification commands succeeded against the exact target digest, and the added per-volume diagnostics are wired to the direct three-OS Pester lane. However, that lane can still false-green container failures, and the shipped consumer-assumption scanner can skip case-distinct files.
